problem: For Poisson–binomial random variables W with variance V, establish a variance-scaled lower bound on the normalized Turán slack δ_D at the first-descent index D of the pmf.
debate: Log-concavity and Turán inequalities for probability mass functions, particularly for Poisson–binomial distributions.
gap: Existing lower bounds on δ_k scale with the number of summands n or the success probabilities and degenerate when summands with probabilities near 0 or 1 accumulate at fixed variance; the literature lacks variance-scaled bounds.
contribution: Theorem 1.1 proves V·δ_D ≥ 1/4 for V ≥ 1, Corollary 1.3 derives exponential tail decay, and Proposition 1.2 shows this constant is tight up to a factor of 4/3.
note: This is a narrow technical refinement: clarify why practitioners should care about variance-scaled Turán slack rather than existing bounds.
